title: Generative AI Alignment with Hinduism’s Theological Plurality and Sacred Representation

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with Bangladeshi Hindu users evaluating how AI-generated scriptural explanations, theological framings, and simulated sacred presence flatten theological plurality and privilege specific traditions over others.

Analyzing participant accounts to identify how generative AI homogenizes diverse regional practices into dominant pan-Hindu templates, misrecognizes local saints, and exoticizes specific sects (e.g., Tantra).
Examining user interactions with AI models to determine how systems sanitize caste into idealized scriptural divisions, thereby erasing lived social hierarchies, exclusions, and regional realities.
Evaluating user feedback on text-to-image outputs that demonstrate colorism and Eurocentric aesthetic standards, specifically the visual whitening of traditionally dark-complexioned deities.
